# Setup

```{r}
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(sdmTMB)
library(sf)
library(patchwork)
library(ggeffects)
ggplot2::theme_set(ggsidekick::theme_sleek())
```

Load data and see what it looks like.

```{r eval=TRUE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE}
d <- read_csv(here(paste0("output/all-snake-skin-data-2026.csv")))
glimpse(d)


```


```{r data,fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="100%"}
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude,
    alpha = as.factor(present),
    colour = common.name
  ))

ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude,
    alpha = as.factor(present),
    colour = museum
  ))

ggplot(d) + geom_histogram(aes(year, fill = card.photo)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept =round(mean(d$year))) +
  facet_wrap(~common.name)

round(mean(d$year))
table(d$species)
table(d$museum, d$species)
```

# Data filtering

There are some spatial outliers in the south that should be removed. Let's try a cutoff of 25 degrees latitude.
There also are relatively few records for Black-crested Titmouse, so we'll drop them from the more complex analyses.
But to start with we can leave them in to see how they fit in with the others. 
Although the overall mean for the whole dataset (black vertical lines) falls near 1950, the majority of temporal coverage is in cards so we'll place our year intercept closer to the centre of the card coverage to reduce leverage. Let's try 1925.

```{r}
d <- d |> filter(latitude > 25)
```

# Generate spatial model

For the spatial models and plotting we will use the Albers projection centered on North America.
```{r}
Albers <- "+proj=aea +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-96 +lat_1=20 +lat_2=60 +x_0=0 +y_0=0
+datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs"
```

We add these projected UTMs to our data and build a mesh from them that will be used in our model.
Using a minimum distance of 100 km given the sparse sampling in much of the continent. 

```{r}
d <- sdmTMB::add_utm_columns(d, utm_crs = Albers)
mesh <- make_mesh(d, xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 80)
plot(mesh)
```

This model includes all species, type of observation (card vs. photo), and a linear scaled year effect that is not allowed to vary in space. I tried models where the year effect could vary in space, but those models didn't converg if allowed to interact with species, or didn't improve AIC if shared across species. 
I tried a random intercept for museum but that model didn't work. 
Allowing anisotropy means that spatial correlations can be asymmetrical. 
Spatially-varying effects allow each species to have it's own spatial pattern. 

```{r run-model, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# sd(d$year)
# [1] 51.98258
d$year_sd <- 50
d$year_centered <- d$year - 1925
d$year_scaled <- d$year_centered / d$year_sd

d$museum <- as.factor(d$museum)
d$common.name <- as.factor(d$common.name)

m_full <- sdmTMB(present~common.name*year_scaled + card.photo,
            time = "common.name",
            spatial = "on",
            spatiotemporal = "iid",
            spatial_varying = ~year_scaled:common.name,
            share_range = FALSE,
            anisotropy = TRUE,
            family = binomial(),
            mesh = mesh,
            data = d
)
```

```{r, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
d$year_sd <- 50
d$year_centered <- d$year - 1925
d$year_scaled <- d$year_centered / d$year_sd

d$museum <- as.factor(d$museum)
d$common.name <- as.factor(d$common.name)

m_no_time <- readRDS(here::here("output/model-no-time.rds"))
m <- readRDS(here::here("output/model-svc.rds"))
# m <- readRDS(here::here("output/model-time.rds")) # no svc
m_full <- readRDS(here::here("output/model-svc-full.rds")) # separate svc for year for each species

tidy(m_full, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(m_full, effects = "ran_pars", conf.int = TRUE)
tidy(m, effects = "ran_pars", conf.int = TRUE)
```


Model checks
```{r, message=TRUE, fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="50%"}
# m
sanity(m_full)
plot_anisotropy(m_full)
plot_anisotropy(m)
```

# Plotting main effects

Simple model with all species but no effect of time. Allowing each species to have it's own spatial field. A model with a shared spatial field is an option, and does converge, but seems less appropriate/realistic to me. 

```{r main_no_time, fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="70%"}
ggeffects::ggeffect(m_no_time, terms =c("common.name", "card.photo")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(colour = group), position = position_dodge(width=0.3)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(y = "Probability snake skin present", colour = "Source") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
```


Add effect of time with interactions allowing each species it's own trend through time and a share spatial field for change over time.

```{r main_w_time, echo = FALSE,fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="70%"}
ggeffects::ggeffect(m, terms =c("common.name", "card.photo")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(colour = group), position = position_dodge(width=0.3)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(y = "Probability snake skin present", colour = "Source") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
```


```{r interactions-m, fig.align = "center", echo = FALSE,fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="70%"}
ggeffects::ggeffect(m, terms =c("year_scaled", "common.name")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x, predicted, fill = group)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels= function(x) x*50 + 1925) +
  labs(y = "Probability snake skin present", colour ="", fill = "") +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
```

Add separate spatial fields for each species' change over time. Best AIC, but not well estimated. I will plot it for interest, but recommend using the previous one for inference. 

```{r main_full, echo = FALSE,fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="70%"}
ggeffects::ggeffect(m_full, terms =c("common.name", "card.photo")) %>%

```

```{r interactions-full, fig.align = "center", echo = FALSE,fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="70%"}
  geom_line(aes(colour = group)) +
```

```{r, echo = FALSE,eval = FALSE, fig.asp = 0.5, out.width="100%"}
# by hand
nd <- data.frame(
  common.name = "Bewick's Wren",
  card.photo = as.factor("card"),

p <- predict(m, newdata = nd, se_fit = TRUE, re_form = NA)

ggplot(p, aes((year_scaled*50 + 1925), plogis(est),
```

# Plotting spatial predictions

To produce pretty maps of these predictions, back transform the spatial coordinates into the same units as our original projection and then convert back into an sf object so that the plot axis will be in latitude and longitude. 

```{r proj-p}
d_noyr <- m$data |> mutate(year_scaled = 0)
pred <- predict(m, newdata = d_noyr, re_form_iid = NA)
p <- pred %>% mutate(X = X * 1000, Y = Y * 1000)
p_proj <- p %>%
  mutate(x = X, y = Y) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = Albers)
```

We can retrieve continental coastlines from the package rnaturalearth and outlines of the great lakes from <https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/110m-physical-vectors/> and transform them to the correct projection. 

```{r shapes}
coast <- rnaturalearth::ne_coastline(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  sf::st_transform(crs = Albers)
lakes <- sf::st_read(here::here("data/ne_110m_lakes"), quiet = TRUE)
lakes <- lakes[lakes$scalerank == 0, ] %>% sf::st_transform(crs = Albers) # only large lakes
```


## Predicted probability present by species 
Model with species-specific trends but shared spatial effect of time.
Estimates represent 1925. 

```{r plot-fixed-effects, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, cache=FALSE, fig.asp = 1.5, out.width="100%"}
ggplot(data = filter(p_proj, year > 1800)) +
  geom_sf(data = coast, colour = "gray50") +
  geom_sf(data = lakes, colour = "gray50", fill = NA) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(min(p_proj$X) - 50000, max(p_proj$X) - 50000),
    ylim = c(min(p_proj$Y), max(p_proj$Y))
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = p, aes(X, Y, colour = plogis(est)),
    alpha = 0.75,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    guide = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")
  ) +
  labs(colour = "Probability \npresent") +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~common.name, ncol = 2)
```



## Spatially varying effect of year

We can extract the overall coefficients using the `b <- tidy(m)` and add them together with the spatially varying coefficients `zeta_s`.
However, this method does not give us spatially explicit estimates of uncertainty.
To do this, we can get the output from the joint precision matrix simulation draws by using the `predict()` function again, but this time indicating a number of simulation draws (e.g., `sims = 500`) and what component we want estimated (`sims_var = "zeta_s"`). 
We also extract the same number of draws for estimates of the main effect using the `spread_sims()` function (this time `n_sims = 500`). 
The simulation draws for both can then be combined before calculating the median and lower and upper quantiles from these draws and adding these values to our predicted data.

```{r proj-p-m-time}
d_noyr <- m_full$data |> mutate(year_scaled = 0)
pred <- predict(m_full, newdata = d_noyr, re_form_iid = NA)
p <- pred %>% mutate(X = X * 1000, Y = Y * 1000)

n_sims <- 500L
zeta_sim <- predict(m_full, nsim = n_sims, sims_var = "zeta_s")
omega_sim <- predict(m_full, nsim = n_sims, sims_var = "omega_s")
sims <- spread_sims(m_full, nsim = n_sims)
```

Create function for spatial coefficient plots with uncertainty
```{r plot-map-function, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, cache=FALSE}
plot_spatial_effect <- function(combined, which_species = "bewr") {

p_proj <- p %>%
  mutate(x = X, y = Y) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = Albers)

p$year_scaled_sim <- apply(combined, 2, median)
p$year_scaled_lwr <- apply(combined, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)
p$year_scaled_upr <- apply(combined, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
p_spp <- filter(p, species == which_species)

  ggformat <- function(dat){
ggplot(data = dat) +
  geom_sf(data = coast, colour = "gray50") +
  geom_sf(data = lakes, colour = "gray50", fill = NA) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(min(p_proj$X) - 50000, max(p_proj$X) - 50000), # adjusts space on sides
    ylim = c(min(p_proj$Y), max(p_proj$Y)-500000)
  ) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    trans = ggsidekick::fourth_root_power_trans(), 
    option = "turbo",
    limit = c(-1000, 150),
    guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top")
  ) +
  guides(size = "none") +
  # labs(colour = "Estimated effect in link space") +
  labs(colour = "Estimated percent change in \nprobability over 25 years") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.4, 0.87), axis.title = element_blank()
  )
  }
    # dividing all values by 2 to shorten interval to 25 years
p0 <- ggformat(p_spp) + geom_point(
    aes(X, Y, colour = year_scaled_sim/2), alpha = 0.75 
  )

p1 <- 
ggformat(p_spp) + geom_point( 
  aes(X, Y, colour = year_scaled_lwr/2), alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  guides(size = "none", colour = "none") +
  ggtitle("Lower 95% CI") 

p2 <- ggformat(p_spp) +
  geom_point(
    aes(X, Y, colour = year_scaled_upr/2), alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  guides(size = "none", colour = "none") +
  ggtitle("Upper 95% CI") 

p0 /(p1 + p2) + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1,0.5))
}
```

## All effects of year for Bewicks Wren
```{r plot-bewr, echo=F, eval=TRUE, height = 6, out.width="100%", cache=FALSE}
beta <- sims$year_scaled
combined <- (1 - exp(beta + t(zeta_sim$`year_scaled:common.nameBewick's Wren`)))*100 # natural space scaled to Bewick's
plot_spatial_effect(combined, which_species = "bewr")
```


## All effects of year for Great-crested Flycatcher
```{r plot-gcfl, echo=F, eval=TRUE, height = 6, out.width="100%", cache=FALSE}
beta <- sims$common.nameGreat.crested.Flycatcher.year_scaled
combined <- (1 - exp(beta + t(zeta_sim$`year_scaled:common.nameGreat-crested Flycatcher`)))*100 # % change
plot_spatial_effect(combined, which_species = "gcfl")
```
